The Structural Diagnostic of Colonial
Oppression
The West (Highlands)
Social Gradients
Complex. Features indigenous nobility,
community leaders, and commoners, allowing
some social mobility and mediation.
Institutional Protection
Corporate autonomy. Indigenous republics
offered communal land and legal buffers
against total extraction.
Economic Role
Extractive but mediated. Focused on silver,
local markets, and tribute systems.
The East (Lowlands)
Social Gradients
Polarized. Near total binary between White
masters and Black slaves, with minor
populations of free people of color.
Institutional Protection
Total commodification. Slaves were treated
as rapid-consumption capital inputs with
zero institutional shielding.
Economic Role
Agro-industrial machine. Sugar and coffee
plantations serving directly the European
world-system.

The Haitian Archetype
Before 1808, the ultimate popular revolution succeeded in the heart of the
capitalist Caribbean. Saint-Domingue is not an anomaly; it is the four-phase
blueprint for the destruction of the colonial order in the Americas.

necessity forced from the bottom up. The

The Structural Reality
1. Independence was the collision of the
"Neoclassical Offensive" against local,
autonomous popular demands.
2. The "People" were fragmented, acting
on localized grievances (tribute,
slavery, land) rather than unified
Enlightenment ideals.
3. The Haitian Archetype reveals the
ultimate truth: The most radical
outcome was not new states, but the
physical dismantling of the colonial
export economy from the bottom up.
The revolution was not the blueprint
of the founders; it was the physical
dismantling of the colonial machine.
